function: Learned RNN optimizer produces downlink beamformers for SDMA, NOMA, and 1- and 2-layer RSMA under sum-rate or min-rate criteria, with a distributed cell-free form (p. 1, 8, 10).
system: MISO downlink: BS with 2 to 64 antennas, 2 to 64 single-antenna users, no RIS, band not stated; cell-free form derived, not simulated (p. 3, 10-13).
method: Learning to optimize: RNN optimizer (two LSTM cells, about 5,000 parameters) on gradients, coordinatewise, with projection; meta-trained offline on the cumulative objective (p. 6, 8, 11).
data_channel: Synthetic i.i.d. complex Gaussian channel, SNR uniform 0 to 20 dB, one realization per epoch; tested on separate samples of the same distribution (p. 8, 11).
test_conditions: Trained at u1=u2=1 and tested over priority ratios 10^-3 to 10^3; trained at N=K=64 and tested with K from 16 to 64 and other SNRs (p. 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: RZF, RZF-SVD, and W-MMSE (baseline code adapted from a public repository); no learned beamforming method compared (p. 11-12).
metrics: Sum rate, min rate, rate region, training curves, steps to converge, wall-clock run time (p. 11-13).
complexity: Inference O(TNK) with T iterations; about 5,000 learnable parameters; 100 steps take 0.15 s (CPU) to 0.86 s (GPU) against 2 to 45 s for W-MMSE (p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 11: "a new channel matrix with i.i.d. Gaussian entries is sampled in each epoch". Training and test channels come from the authors' own synthetic Gaussian model (p. 8); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 13: "a single RNN is trained for the case N = K = 64 and then tested with different values of K and SNR"; p. 12: "The RNN was trained only for the case u1 = u2 = 1 and tested over the range of u2" (Fig. 6).
q3_support: p. 11: "As baseline beamforming methods, we consider regularized zero-forcing (RZF)" and W-MMSE: non-learned only. No earlier learned beamformer (meta-learning RSMA precoder, unfolded WMMSE) is run; the paper only discusses them (p. 2, 9).
q4_support: p. 11: "Since the RNN operates coordinatewise, the computational complexity is O(T N K) where T is the number of iterations", with about 5,000 learnable parameters; Table I (p. 12) gives wall-clock run times against W-MMSE.
q5_support: p. 11 (footnote 3): "The training code was adapted from" a third-party GitHub repository on learning to learn by gradient descent; the paper links no code or data of its own, and the training data are simulated Gaussian channels.
notes: Title on page 1 is 'RNN Beamforming Optimizer for Rate-Splitting Multiple Access and Cell-Free Massive MIMO' with DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2024.3486982, so the PDF matches. Included as a learned beamformer: the RNN parameters are meta-trained (p. 6, 8), so it is not a classical iteration; area 3 (BS precoder). The cell-free scheme is derived in Section V (p. 9-10) but no cell-free result is simulated; all results are for a single BS. Perfect CSI is assumed at inference (p. 2). Table I was read from the page image (p. 12).
